Step 1: Understand the historical context of the U.S. civil rights movement regarding bus segregation.
Step 2: Identify the famous individuals who refused to give up their bus seats to white passengers in Montgomery, Alabama.
Step 3: Recall that while Rosa Parks became the most famous symbol of the Montgomery bus boycott in December 1955, a 15-year-old girl named Claudette Colvin was actually arrested for the same offense nine months earlier, on March 2, 1955, making her the first person to be arrested for this specific resistance in Montgomery.
Step 4: Match this historical fact to the provided options. Option (B) correctly identifies Claudette Colvin as the first person.

Final answer: B
